**BLOCKING.** Condition: any machine whose temp directory is reached through a symbolic link — macOS, where `TMPDIR` sits under `/var/folders` (`/var` -> `private/var`) and `/tmp` -> `/private/tmp`. That is the condition your own comment at lines 1216-1219 names, eighteen lines above.

`frozen` is built from `repository`, which descends from `Path(tempfile.TemporaryDirectory())` and is never resolved, while the grid prints the resolved spelling (`record_names.REPO_ROOT` is `Path(__file__).resolve()...`). So `str(frozen) in result.stdout` is False on a run that is correct.

Measured, not argued: with `TMPDIR` pointed at a symbolic link on this Linux box, `python3 scripts/cold-read-grid-test.py` exits 1 with exactly this one case failing — `1 case(s) failed: the line names the copy that changed, not the untouched original` — and the failure detail shows the printed line carrying the resolved path while the check holds the symlinked one. With `TMPDIR` at a real directory the suite passes, and the full sweep at this head is 68/68.

The two checks above already do the right thing; this one wants `str(frozen.resolve()) in result.stdout`.

body:
Non-blocking. Condition: the ORIGINAL is edited during a run and the frozen copy is not — now the ordinary case, since the /cold-read operator is often revising the draft while the cells run.

Marking the set and exiting 3 is right, and so is reusing the existing marker. What is no longer true is the sentence `mark_reports_target_changed` builds and stamps into every report: "Which text any one report in this directory describes is unknown: the edit may have landed before a given reviewer opened the file or after." After this change that cannot happen — every report describes the frozen copy, whose bytes are in the record and did not move. The run knows which text each report describes and tells its reader it does not, permanently, in a record that is kept.

That is the rule the function's own comment sets: "these cold-read-records are kept, so a sentence claiming more than the check knows would outlive the run."

This does not need a new marker. `TARGET_CHANGED_MARKER_PREFIX` is a fixed prefix and the detail is free text after it, so the sentence can turn on `changed_path` while everything downstream still recognises the marker.

Non-blocking. Condition: a caller that branches on this program's exit code, or an operator reading its `--help`.

The module docstring is this program's help text (`ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)`), and its exit-code table defines 2 as "bad invocation (including a cold-read-target this instrument refuses to review)". A freeze that did not happen is neither: the invocation was good and nothing was refused. 2 is a fair choice for "nothing ran", but the table does not cover this case, so 2 now means two different things and the docstring names only one.

body:
**Relative references in the cold-read-target stop resolving for the cold-read-cells.**

Failing condition: the target links to another file by a path relative to its own directory, such as `](../issues/46-ghi-info-agent-design.md)`. The cells are now given `cold-read-records/<record>/target/<repo path>` (this line), so `..` resolves inside the record's `target/` tree. The linked file is not there.

Examples that resolve today from their own directory and would not from the copy (checked with `ls` at this head):
- `docs/drafts/ghi-info-agent-plan-draft.md` → `../issues/46-ghi-info-agent-design.md`, `../issues/26-dynamic-agent-team-model.md`
- `docs/drafts/ghi-write-skill-draft.md` → `../../.claude/skills/ghi-write/SKILL.md`
- `docs/agents/doctrine-instructions.md` → `../nedschorus-wiki/nedschorus-agent-seat-model.md`

Twenty-five `.md` files under `docs/` and `.claude/skills/` contain `../` or `./` relative references.

Effect: the defect-hunt and terminology prompts limit each cell's context to "whatever that document references by an explicit path". A cell can no longer open those references, so it loses the context the author supplied. It may also report them as unresolved or unexplained references (defect-hunt class (d)) when they are correct in the repository. Meanwhile `reference_integrity_pre_pass` (line 300) checks against the original's directory (`target.parent / clean`) and marks the same references `ok` in `reference-check.md`, so the record contradicts itself.

The cause is the retarget to the copy, so this PR triggers it. Any fix that restores resolution against the original's directory would close it. One option: tell each cell the original's repository path, so it resolves relative references from there and still reads only the copy's bytes.

body:
**Relative links in the target stop resolving for every cold-read-cell.**

The condition: the cold-read-target links a sibling or parent file by a relative path. Each cell is now handed `<record>/target/<repository path>`, and only the target itself is copied there, so the link points at a file that doesn't exist.

Reproduced:
- `docs/drafts/ghi-info-agent-plan-draft.md:16` links `ghi-gatekeeper-plan-draft.md`, which exists only beside the original.
- `docs/drafts/ghi-write-skill-draft.md` links `../../.claude/skills/ghi-write/SKILL.md`.
- About 25 `.md` files under `docs/` and `.claude/skills/` contain such links.

The cells' prompts limit their context to what the document references by explicit path. So a cell loses the context the author linked, and it may report correct links as unresolved. Meanwhile `reference_integrity_pre_pass` resolves the same links against the original's directory and marks them `ok`, so the record contradicts itself.

The fix: keep handing each cell the frozen copy, and also name the original's repository path, with the instruction to resolve relative references from the original's directory. The cells still read frozen text, and the links the author wrote still resolve.

body:
**The new paragraph sends paths written from the repository root to the wrong directory.**

This paragraph tells every cell to "Resolve every relative path the document references from {target_origin.parent}".

The condition: the target sits in a subdirectory and cites a path written from the repository root, which is this repository's normal citation form. The cell is then told to look in, for example, `docs/drafts/scripts/foo.py`, which doesn't exist. Before this commit, cells ran with `cwd=REPO_ROOT` (`:1136`), so those paths resolved naturally.

The scale: 87 `.md` files under `docs/` and `.claude/skills/` cite, in backticks, a path that exists from the root but not from the file's own directory. One is `docs/nedschorus-wiki/nedschorus-sdlc-terms.md`, which cites `docs/nedschorus-wiki/nedschorus-glossary.md`.

The grid's own pre-pass (`cold-read-grid.py:308`) resolves each path from `REPO_ROOT` **or** `target.parent`, so it marks these `ok` while every cell is sent elsewhere. That is the self-contradiction the previous round blocked, now for the more common form.

To fix it, make the paragraph say what the pre-pass does: resolve each relative path from the repository root, or failing that, from the original's directory. Read the copy for the text only.
